title: Antwerp-Central railway station
exportLabel: Molen original Antwerp-Central historic headhouse and train shed shared-surface source
visualBrief: Complete historic passenger headhouse plus connected 187m barrel-vaulted train shed. Whole 253m parent plan. Include side wings and mansards, two faceted pavilions with domes and pierced lanterns, glazed entrance screen and clock, large arched fanlight and domed central hall/lantern, real open street-level entrance arcades, and shed roof/end/side framing. Original approximate ornament and hidden windows; no logos, copied sculptures, navigable interior or train stock. Southern platform extensions and modern canopies remain native.

Skyline keeps the full connected plan, open coarse arcade and lantern silhouettes, with thin post plates and flat window bands. District adds individual opening patches and pavilion detail. Street adds real window recesses, shallow frames and shed ribs. Close-up refines curves, frames, ribs and original geometric ornament; master preserves finer curves separately.

references.observed: Complete north-front elevated picture actually inspected: pale rusticated masonry, red-brick side returns, multiple open arcade bays at street level, two projecting faceted corner pavilions with round windows, tall windowed upper stages, domed slate roofs and pierced lanterns, a central multi-story glazed screen and round clock. A broad high arched fanlight and large domed roof with gold-capped lantern rise behind the glazed entrance. Side wings have closed mansard/slate roofs, dormers, rectangular windows and pale cornices. Ornament is simplified original geometry; do not copy lettering or statues.

Whole station aerial from the south actually inspected: long connected barrel-vaulted train shed with dark muted glass panels, reddish iron arch/end framing, straight side walls and longitudinal roof bands. It terminates behind the ornate domed passenger headhouse. Rail approaches continue south beyond the principal shed. Tall modern hotels and neighboring streets/zoo remain independent context, not parts of the historic station model.
